newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico '97 tortilla subsidies 8.3 bln pesos - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico '97 tortilla subsidies 8.3 bln pesos - paper.

text.p: Mexico's staple food agency Conasupo will subsidize corn pancake tortillas to the tune of 8.321 billion pesos in 1997, daily Reforma reported Wednesday.
Citing a Conasupo report, Reforma said the subsidies will allow price controls on tortillas to continue.
Of the total, 3.113 billion pesos will go to subsidise 2.8 million tonnes of corn flour processed by Grupo Industrial Maseca, Minsa, Agroinsa and Amasa.
Conasupo will spend another 5.208 billion pesos buying 2.6 million tonnes of corn from farmers at floor prices set in each state, Reforma said.

Reforma said the report highlighted that the tortilla production chain consumed between 6 million and 7 million tonnes of corn per year. It said 2.2 million tonnes went to Maseca, 600,000 to Minsa and 200,000 tonnes to Agroinsa and Amasa.
Maseca has 19 corn flour processing plants, Minsa has six plants and Agroinsa and Amasa both have one plant each, Reforma said.
Another 3.4 million tonnes of corn is consumed directly by around 10,000 individual corn mills which supply around private 40,000 tortilla makers and outlets around the country.
